paper_summary: Archaeological conservation science paper (Int. J. Conservation Science 17(1), 2026) on a Late Period polychrome wooden coffin excavated at Rass Algesr, Saqqara, Egypt. OM, SEM-EDX, Raman and FTIR identified the pigments (yellow ochre/goethite and orpiment, Egyptian blue/cuprorivaite, hematite red, calcite white, carbon black), a calcium carbonate ground layer, a linen fabric layer and animal glue binder. Conservation comprised mechanical and chemical cleaning, consolidation with Klucel G, reattachment of the gesso with 10% Primal AC33, and filling the gesso edges with glass microballoons in 15% w/v Paraloid B72 in acetone.
extraction_notes: Off-topic for syntactic foam Process-Structure-Property extraction. The only hollow-particle content is a conservation filler: 'Using a spatula, glass microballoons containing Paraloid B72 in 15% w/v acetone were applied. The microballoons were then coated with earth pigments.' (Sec. 'Filling the edges of the ground layer', p. 54, repeated in the Conclusion). This is a gap-filling putty applied by hand to an artefact, not a characterized hollow-particle composite: no particle grade, size, density, volume or weight fraction, no foam density, and no mechanical, thermal or any other property measurement of the microballoon/Paraloid mixture is reported anywhere in the paper. The paper's only quantitative material data concern pigment chemistry (EDX elements, Raman/FTIR band positions), painted-layer thickness (100 micron), and consolidant concentrations (Klucel G 0.5% and 1% in ethyl alcohol, Primal AC33 10%, Paraloid B72 15% w/v, ethanol:water 1:1).
